name: Choline supplements
short: Healthy volunteers: choline bitartrate raised TMAO, platelet reactivity (lab markers) in one trial; another saw no TMAO change. Children with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder: fishy odour 36% vs 8%.
text: In three pooled placebo-controlled trials in 104 children aged 2.5 to 5.9 years with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder, given choline for 9 months, adverse effects were similar between groups except fishy body odour (36% with choline versus 8% with placebo). In a randomised placebo-controlled trial in 70 heavily drinking pregnant women given 2 g of choline a day until delivery, the only side effect was a small increase in nausea or indigestion, with no effect on diarrhoea, vomiting, blood pressure or body odour; the abstract does not report pregnancy or birth outcomes. TMAO is a gut-microbe product of choline that one study's authors describe as prothrombotic and proatherogenic: in healthy volunteers with normal kidney function, 4 weeks of choline bitartrate supplements raised plasma TMAO and platelet reactivity in all three study arms that included them, while eggs and phosphatidylcholine supplements did not; in a separate crossover trial in 30 healthy young adults, about 400 mg of choline a day for 4 weeks, from a supplement or from eggs, did not change plasma TMAO. Neither abstract reports clinical events such as heart attacks or blood clots. An older review stated that high intakes of choline or lecithin produce acute gastrointestinal distress, sweating, salivation and loss of appetite, judged lasting harm from self-administration improbable, and raised a concern about depression with prolonged high intakes of lecithin. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
